notes: Same access route/method as bs168 (direct HTTP, no block). Full catalog-tree search (see bs168 notes) found 'New In' (/c/whats-new-14571) as a top-level nav item under 'Shop All', matching the homepage nav (13 occurrences of 'new-arrivals'/'whats-new' in embedded menu data). 'New In' has exactly one child, 'All New Arrivals' (/c/whats-new-14571/new-arrivals) - a real product-grid PLP with sort/filter, genuinely representing recently-added catalogue items (not a lookbook/campaign page). The parent 'New In' node's own direct-category API query returned totalResults=0 (it is a pure nav-landing wrapper with no products assigned directly to it), the same pattern the prior Home-Decor pass documented for other group-only parent nodes on this platform (e.g. 'Lighting', 'Wall Decor and Mirrors', 'Home Accessories' parents all had qty=None). Since there is only one genuine child and the parent carries no listing of its own, this is reported as a single undifferentiated row (per brief section 3: 'If only a single New Arrivals listing exists, output just that one row') using the child's URL, which is where the actual products live. No department-specific ('Furniture New Arrivals', etc.) or Crate & Kids-specific New Arrivals sub-listings exist anywhere in the 550+-node catalog tree.
